Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
articles.abstract: Abstract Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Unidirectional rolling of single-crystal graphene into nanoscrolls
Rethinking Klebsiella pneumoniae vaccines: from protective immunity to rational vaccine design
articles.abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae infections cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually, yet a licensed vaccine remains elusive. Current strategies targeting capsular polysaccharides and lipopolysaccharides show promise but face limitations due to the complexity of Klebsiella pathogenesis and incomplete understanding of protective immunity. This Review highlights the critical barriers hindering broad protection against K. pneumoniae . We argue that next-generation vaccines require a paradigm shift, integrating antigen discovery, systems immunology and translational models to define conserved protective targets and immune correlates. This holistic strategy is essential to predict vaccine efficacy and finally combat this escalating global health threat.

articles.title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
articles.abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

articles.title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
articles.abstract: Abstract Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8 + T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm ). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti- Lm CD8 + T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8 + T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm . These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

articles.title: Diminished subsurface oxygen maximum linked to rapid decline of the North Pacific Central Mode Water
3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
articles.abstract: Abstract Investigating the movements and conformational changes of proteins in living cells is essential for understanding their function. The recently introduced fluorescence nanoscopy method called MINSTED has successfully tracked single fluorophore-labelled proteins, albeit in fixed cells and two dimensions only. Here we introduce a MINSTED setup for live-cell tracking of individual proteins in three dimensions (3D) with a localization precision σ down to <1 nm. Applied to the motor protein kinesin-1, our MINSTED nanoscope follows single proteins in 3D as they process along microtubules in 16 nm steps. Individual steps are resolved amid substantial intracellular background. The unique capability of the 3D stimulated emission depletion (STED) beam to carve out the signal of the protein label of interest enables efficient single-molecule investigations at hitherto unpractically high concentrations of labelled proteins and thus in crowded live-cell environments.

articles.title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
Programmable synaptic and stochastic regimes in a monolayer hBN atomristor
Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
articles.abstract: Abstract Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

articles.title: Distinct mechanisms of CNV formation at the human 15q13.3 locus
Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
articles.abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4 + Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4 + Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Combination of PARP and KRASG12D inhibitors enhances therapeutic efficacy by exploiting vulnerabilities in PDAC
Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
articles.abstract: Abstract A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells

Heatwaves Trigger
Nonlinear Rises in Nonmethane Hydrocarbons
articles.abstract: Abstract Urban heatwaves intensify ozone and particulate pollution by accelerating volatile organic compound (VOC) oxidation in the presence of nitrogen oxides (NOx). However, the temperature dependence of anthropogenic nonmethane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) remains poorly constrained and may become strongly nonlinear under extreme heat. The temperature response of anthropogenic VOC emissions depends on species-specific physicochemical properties. Here, we show that anthropogenic NMHC concentrations measured in Guangzhou, China, exhibit two distinct temperature thresholds at 26.5 °C (associated with the dew point) and near 30 °C (associated with an effective volatility threshold), above which concentrations increase abruptly. Using high-resolution observations, statistical classification, and thermodynamic simulations, we show that these thresholds arise from coupled volatility and chemical-reactivity effects that link phase behavior to atmospheric chemical loss. Chemical depletion accelerates with warming but exhibits diminishing marginal sensitivity, while ambient NMHCs volatilize in three hierarchical batches ordered by boiling point. These nonlinear concentration responses are not captured by traditional steady-state emission parametrizations that assume simple linear temperature scaling. Incorporating threshold-based volatilization behavior into urban chemistry models should improve predictions of ozone formation and particulate pollution during heatwaves and under future climate warming.

articles.title:
Redox
Perturbations
Promote Oxidative and Cometabolic
Reaction Networks for Enhanced Organic Micropollutant Removal in Activated
Sludge
articles.abstract: Abstract Understanding how redox conditions shape enzyme expression and micropollutant transformation in activated sludge remains a key challenge. Here, we show that engineered redox perturbation enriches enzymatic guilds that shape not only the extent of organic micropollutant (OMP) removal but the type and coupling of reaction pathways. Dynamic oxic–anoxic cycling at 2 or 7 mg/L dissolved oxygen, with nominal 3- or 6 min periods, restructured enzyme expression and expanded transformation chemistry beyond that of steady aeration. Integrating SWATH-MS metaproteomics with Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) paired mass distance (PMD) reactomics across 30 OMPs, we resolved condition-specific enzyme upregulation: OxyR-associated catalase-peroxidase induction (EC 1) under high-DO cycling tracked oxygenation-type PMDs ([+O], [+2O], [+3O]), whereas transferase (EC 2) and hydrolase (EC 3) upregulation tracked methylation, acylation, and bond-cleavage signatures. Perturbation significantly upregulated 18 PMD types over continuous aeration, expanded OMP reaction networks, and drove removal gains up to 63% for macrolides and 49% for nitrogen heterocycles, whereas benzotriazole, diclofenac, and carbendazim declined, possibly through NADPH competition. Class-level guild analysis linked Proteobacterial and Nitrospira enzymes to functional-group-selective transformations, with perturbation mainly redistributing each class’s contribution to shared enzyme pools. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for tailoring redox regimes in existing systems to enhance OMP removal.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Humic
and Fulvic Acids Elicit Distinct Multi-Organ
and Microbial Responses after Chronic Oral Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Humic acid (HA) and fulvic acid (FA) are major constituents of natural organic matter (NOM) that can exhibit dynamic supramolecular and colloidal organization in aqueous environments. Given the widespread occurrence of NOM in environmental waters and that untreated natural water can represent a chronic oral exposure source for wildlife and populations lacking safely managed drinking water, the intrinsic biological effects of HA and FA after chronic oral exposure remain insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted a 90-day multidose oral mouse exposure integrating histopathology, biochemistry, gut microbiome profiling, and untargeted metabolomics to evaluate responses to Suwannee River humic acid (SRHA) and fulvic acid (SRFA). Both substances were associated with lipid-related metabolic alterations, intestinal mucosal changes, neural alterations, and oxidative-stress-related responses. SRHA, with higher aromaticity and apparent molecular weight, showed broader gut microbial changes, whereas SRFA, with lower apparent molecular weight and higher polarity, showed broader metabolic alterations in serum, liver, and brain. Multiomics integration revealed distinct microbiota–metabolome associations, while complementary interface assays suggested that structural and interfacial differences may contribute to these response patterns. These findings demonstrate distinct biological responses to chronic SRHA and SRFA exposure, supporting further consideration of the intrinsic bioactivity of humic substances in environmental exposure assessment.

articles.title: Fe–N x -Coordinated Algal Carbon with CaS for Enhanced and Extended Dechlorination of Chlorinated Hydrocarbons by Zero-Valent Iron
articles.abstract: Abstract Sulfidation improves the electron selectivity of zero-valent iron (ZVI), whereas Fe–Nx coordination structures could lower intrinsic dechlorination energy barriers. However, the synergistic integration of these two functionalities and their cooperative mechanism remain unclear. Here, we synthesized an algae-derived carbon material (Fex@NBC) containing both Fe–Nx sites and CaS via pyrolysis of iron-laden algal sludge. Upon coupling with nanoscale ZVI (nZVI), CaS-induced in situ sulfidation generated FeSx at the Fe0 surface, forming a dual-functional architecture with FeSx and Fe–Nx sites. The Fex@NBC/nZVI system achieved 84.3% of trichloroethylene (TCE) dechlorination within 24 h with a rate constant of 0.12 h–1 and an electron efficiency of 80.5%. Notably, 23.8% of the recalcitrant 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCA) was degraded within 50 days, demonstrating an extended dechlorination boundary. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Fe–Nx sites serve as the primary catalytic centers, while FeSx enhances interfacial electron transfer from Fe0 to Fe–Nx and suppresses hydrogen evolution. The cooperative regulation of catalytic activation and electron utilization remains effective under aging, ion influence, and realistic groundwater conditions. This work provides a resource-recovery concept for valorizing iron-enriched algal sludge while revealing the cooperative mechanism between Fe–Nx catalysis and FeSx-mediated electron regulation in ZVI-based remediation systems.

articles.title:
Precipitation-Modulated
Differential Scavenging of
Atmospheric Nitric Acid, Nitrogen Dioxide, and Particulate Nitrate:
Isotopic Constraints on Wet Nitrate Sources
articles.abstract: Abstract Quantifying the relative contributions of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and gaseous nitric acid (HNO3), and particulate nitrate (p-NO3–) to wet NO3– (w-NO3–) and understanding their differential scavenging remain critical challenges for nitrogen deposition modeling. Traditional approaches often neglect direct NO2 scavenging, introducing source apportionment uncertainties. Here, we compile a global dual-isotope (δ15N, δ18O) data set covering w-NO3– and its three precursors across 91 sites in Asia, North America, and Europe. Using an isotope mass-balance model, we quantify fractional contributions (F values) and preferential scavenging degrees (β values) of each precursor and examine their responses to mean annual precipitation. Average F values for NO2, HNO3, and p-NO3– are 26 ± 18, 39 ± 20, and 35 ± 20%, respectively, while their atmospheric abundance fractions (f values) are 76 ± 12, 9 ± 7, and 15 ± 11%. β values follow a universal order (βHNO3 > βp-NO3– > βNO2), confirming that HNO3 is preferentially scavenged. Precipitation modulates β values species-specifically: βHNO3 decreases with increasing precipitation, whereas βNO2 increases. Notably, our results suggest a tentative shift toward p-NO3– as the dominant precursor of w-NO3– at roughly 1750 mm of mean annual precipitation, although this crossing does not represent a statistically robust threshold. These findings provide quantitative constraints for model parametrization and inform region-specific nitrogen mitigation strategies.

articles.title:
Nationwide Study
of Per-and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances
in Dragonfly Larvae and Water in United States Protected Areas
articles.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread in the environment and are of global concern because of their prevalence, persistence, and toxicity. Information about PFAS on federally protected and Tribal lands is limited, despite calls from scientific and regulatory communities for data on environmental background concentrations. To respond to this, we leveraged an existing citizen-science network to collect dragonfly larvae (n = 179 sites) and water (n = 81 sites) from 108 national parks, national wildlife refuges, forests, and Tribal lands across the continental United States and Puerto Rico. Our results showed that PFAS are widespread, with PFOS and PFBA frequently observed (>60% of samples) in dragonfly larvae and water, respectively. Individual PFAS concentrations ranged from 0.22 to 56.6 ng/L in water and 0.10 to 480 ng/g dry weight in dragonfly larvae. Results from this novel broad-scale assessment indicated that concentrations were greater, and profiles were more diverse, in the eastern compared to western United States. Potential drivers of bioaccumulation were distance to source, habitat type, and land use, and large-scale variation in bioaccumulation was related to ecoregion and precipitation. Information from this study can help identify localized hotspots, prioritize monitoring and modeling efforts, and inform future management strategies.

articles.title:
A
Chain of Multiple Cryptic N-Fe-Mn-CH4 Redox Couplings
in Methanogenic Lake Sediments
articles.abstract: Abstract Approximately 30% of methane (CH4) emissions originate from freshwater sediments, typically oxygen- and sulfate (SO42-)-depleted, limiting their ability to regulate CH4 release. Here, we unravel a chain of triple cryptic N-Mn/Fe-CH4 redox couplings in natural, unpolluted reduced methanogenic lake sediments, which impact their cycles while sustaining complex aerobic and anaerobic microbial communities. Sediment profiles revealed an unexpected increase in nitrite (NO2-) along with elevated Fe2+, Mn2+, active NC10 bacteria, and aerobic methanotrophs and decreased CH4 levels. Sediment incubations amended under anoxic conditions with labeled ammonium (15NH4+) produced 15NO2- and 15N2, indicating anaerobic NH4+ oxidation, likely coupled to Mn(IV)/Fe(III) reduction. We further identified a sink for NO3-/NO2- coupled to Fe2+ oxidation, with Fe2+ partly derived from Fe(III)-dependent CH4 oxidation. The activity of NC10 bacteria and Methylococcales suggests an additional NO2- sink via NO2- disproportionation and potentially dark oxygen production, thereby facilitating aerobic CH4 oxidation under anoxic conditions. These coupled cycles likely dominate sulfate-depleted, organic- and Mn/Fe-rich methanogenic freshwater sediments, including many eutrophic lakes and wetlands that are expected to expand under global warming.

articles.title:
Advanced
Classification of Light-Absorbing Aerosols
Using a Two-Dimensional Absorption Ångström Exponent (2D
AAE) Space
articles.abstract: Abstract Light-absorbing aerosols (LAA) play a critical role in climate forcing and remain one of the largest sources of uncertainty in climate models. Ambient aerosols exhibit complex absorption spectral features making the Absorption Ångström Exponent (AAE) calculation highly sensitive to the chosen wavelength range, which can significantly affect interpretations of aerosol properties and source contribution. This study introduces an advanced classification framework for LAA using multiwavelength absorption measurements and a two-dimensional AAE approach, strengthened by absorption deviation in UV (2D AAE + Δ340). For the first time, continuous field measurements at seven European sites using a new nine-wavelength Aethalometer (AE36s; 340–950 nm) were combined with targeted laboratory experiments to systematically characterize aerosol absorption properties. AAE was calculated over two spectral ranges, AAE400–590 (400, 470, 520, 590 nm) and AAE590–950 (590, 630, 880, 950 nm) and the relative deviation at 340 nm from the AAE400–590-derived power law fit (Δ340) was introduced as an additional metric. The resulting 2D AAE fingerprints enable robust discrimination among fresh and aged black carbon (BCfresh, BCaged), residential and open biomass-burning aerosol (BBres and BBopen), and mineral dust. The proposed 2D AAE approach significantly improves LAA type identification and source apportionment compared with conventional single-range AAE analysis, enhancing interpretation of multiwavelength absorption data and supporting more accurate assessment of aerosol climate and air-quality impacts.

articles.title:
Electron-Withdrawing
Picolinate Substituents Accelerate
Fe(III)/Fe(II) Cycling in Fenton Reactions
articles.abstract: Abstract The Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox cycle is the driving force of Fenton chemistry, governing the generation of reactive oxidants, the efficiency of H2O2 utilization, and the amount of iron sludge. However, rational regulation of Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling remains a long-standing challenge, largely due to the poorly understood relationship between iron electronic structures and iron redox kinetics. Here, using the ferric picolinate complex (FeIII–PICA)-mediated Fenton reaction as a model system, we systematically investigate how the iron electronic structure influences Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling by varying the substituent group on PICA. Electron-withdrawing substituents markedly accelerate Fe(III) reduction, hydroxyl radical generation, and pollutant degradation. The kinetic analysis, combined with theoretical calculations, identifies Fe–O homolysis of the ferric hydroperoxo intermediate (PICA–FeIII–OOH) as the rate-limiting step of Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. Electronic structure analysis reveals that electron-withdrawing substituents narrow the gap of redox-active orbitals of PICA–FeIII–OOH to lower the reaction barrier for Fe–O homolysis. Consequently, this orbital modulation facilitates electron transfer to the iron center and accelerates iron cycling. Furthermore, the energy level of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (ELUMO) serves as a more accessible descriptor that quantitatively captures substituent effects across different substitution types and positions. These findings establish a quantitative structure–reactivity relationship for Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling of Fenton reactions, providing a preliminary design pattern for developing efficient iron-based catalysts.

articles.title:
Rapid
Conversion
of Criegee-Derived Organic Peroxides
into Distinct Organic Nitrogen Products via Interfacial Reaction with
Amines
articles.abstract: Abstract Organic nitrogen (ON) compounds represent a substantial fraction of atmospheric reactive nitrogen, yet the mechanisms governing their secondary formation in the condensed phase remain poorly constrained. In this study, we investigated the interfacial reactions between terpenoid-derived organic peroxides (OPs), specifically α-acyloxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-AAHs) and α-alkoxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-AHs), with common atmospheric amines (ethylamine, dimethylamine, and propylamine) using surface-sensitive mass spectrometry and isotope labeling. Our results demonstrate that α-AAHs react rapidly with amines to form ON products via a nucleophilic addition–elimination mechanism, sharing a common pathway with α-hydroxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-HHs). Notably, α-AAHs exhibit even faster kinetics than α-HHs, with calculated atmospheric half-lives (τ1/2) as short as subminute at 10 ppt amine exposure. In contrast, α-AHs show relatively inert toward amines compared to α-AAHs, and their reactions with ethylamine and dimethylamine proceed via distinct formation pathways. Kinetic analysis reveals that these interfacial interactions are reaction-limited processes, unaffected by variations in interfacial solvent structure. These findings identify direct reactions of Criegee-derived OPs with amines as a potentially rapid pathway to ON formation that may complement conventional carbonyl–amine chemistry. This study highlights a previously underestimated non-negligible source of secondary organic nitrogen, which is essential for accurately assessing aerosol impacts on air quality, human health, and climate forcing.

articles.title:
Resilient
Net Community Production in a Warming North
Pacific Ocean (2001–2019)
articles.abstract: Abstract Net community production (NCP)─carbon fixation remaining after autotrophic and heterotrophic respiration─regulates surface fCO2, air–sea CO2 exchange, and the ocean’s vertical carbon gradient. However, sparse measurements limit our understanding of its long-term variability at basin scales. We estimated North Pacific NCP at 1° × 1° resolution for 2001–2019 from the warming-period (wp) drawdown of dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) in the surface mixed layer. CT was reconstructed from more than 3.3 million surface fCO2 observations and empirically estimated total alkalinity using carbonate-system thermodynamics, with corrections for salinity, net air–sea CO2 exchange, vertical diffusion, and CaCO3 production. Mean NCP was 1.3 ± 0.1 Pg C wp–1 and exhibited no long-term trend despite 0.6 °C of basin-wide warming, which is expected to suppress biological production by strengthening stratification and limiting nutrient supply. This apparent stability masked opposing trends: declining NCP in the western deep-mixed-layer region was offset by increasing NCP in the tropics, potentially supported by enhanced nitrogen fixation. Thus, basin-wide stability reflected regional compensation rather than a uniform response to warming. Nevertheless, a projected NCP decline of approximately 0.16 Pg C yr–1 by 2100 is equivalent in magnitude to approximately 30% of the basin’s current net air–sea CO2 uptake.

articles.title: Advancing a Circular Economy: A Special Issue in Environmental Science & Technology , ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering , and ACS Sustainable Resource Management

Abiotic Methane
Production Driven by Hydrogen Peroxide
Generated during Anoxic–Oxic Transitions in Coastal Sediments
articles.abstract: Abstract Coastal ecosystems are recognized as substantial sources of atmospheric methane (CH4), which has traditionally been attributed to anaerobic methanogenesis by archaea. However, reactive oxygen species (ROS) are known to mediate abiotic CH4 production through iron-mediated Fenton-type chemistry. Whether tidal redox oscillations in coastal sediments generate ROS to drive this pathway naturally remains unknown. Here, we combined slurry incubation experiments under anoxic–oxic transitions with geochemical measurements and metatranscriptomic profiling to investigate hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-driven abiotic CH4 production in mangrove sediments. Upon O2 exposure, anoxically incubated active sediments rapidly produced H2O2 at rates of 9.3–100.7 mmol kgDW–1 h–1. The H2O2 was then consumed within hours, pointing to its role as a reactive intermediate. Concomitantly, O2 exposure significantly enhanced CH4 production in active sediments, with the maximum yields varying from 1.6 to 8.1 times those under continuous N2. Furthermore, inactivated sediments retained CH4 production under O2 exposure, and H2O2 quenching suppressed CH4 production in both active and inactivated sediments. This indicates that a substantial fraction of the CH4 produced upon oxygenation was H2O2-driven rather than of enzymatic origin. Metatranscriptomic analysis revealed that O2 exposure downregulated the transcription of methanogenesis-related genes, further indicating that O2 availability may inversely regulate the biogenic and abiotic contributions to CH4 production. These findings reveal a naturally occurring abiotic CH4 production pathway driven by H2O2 generation during tidal redox oscillations and sustained by abundant endogenous methyl donors, with implications for the global CH4 budget.

articles.title: Nontargeted Metabolomics Reveal Multi-Pathway Disruption from BPA Exposure in the Freshwater Snail Planorbella pilsbryi
articles.abstract: Abstract Bisphenol A (BPA) is used in the production of plastics and resins and is a well-established endocrine disruptor in humans and vertebrates; however, its effects on invertebrates are not understood. This study employed metabolomics to examine the biological effects of BPA exposure in the freshwater pulmonate snail Planorbella pilsbryi after a 28-d exposure at three concentrations (0.13, 3.7, and 479 μg/L). Using nontargeted liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS), we characterized the metabolomic profile of exposure to BPA in P. pilsbryi and identified perturbations to biological pathways. BPA exposure caused a significant increase in the abundance of lipids at all concentrations in whole-tissue homogenates, and numerous biological pathways were dysregulated by BPA, including pathways related to energy, metabolism, and digestion. BPA also decreased the abundance of methylated nucleobases, suggesting changes to DNA and RNA that may affect physiological function and gene expression. Overall, the present study revealed insights into the ways in which BPA affects freshwater pulmonate snails. The findings also serve as a framework for the use of metabolomics as a tool to investigate sublethal end points of effect in a nonmodel species. Additional research, such as targeted approaches oriented by the findings of this study, is needed to elucidate the effects of BPA in aquatic mollusks.

articles.title:
Climate Effect of
Alternative Binders: Life Cycle
Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Potential as a Carbon Sink
articles.abstract: Abstract Substituting Portland cement (PC) with alternative binders offers a promising pathway to mitigate the climate impacts of the cement industry, one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize. While substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are generated during production, most alternative binders can sequester CO2 during their service life. This effect has been acknowledged from a technical perspective, yet its significant influences on the GHG footprint of alternative binders remain unresolved. In this study, we quantify the CO2 uptake of common alternative binders alongside their lifetime GHG emissions. We demonstrate that most binders can take up a larger amount of CO2 than PC during usage, due to a thermodynamically high uptake capacity or high uptake kinetics. The uptake reactions enable a dynamic CO2 loop, with 1–248% of the production emissions being recovered over a 100-year structure service life. However, when the slow reaction rate is considered, the associated climate benefits can be up to 71% lower than the theoretical apparent uptake value. Our results highlight the importance of combined CO2 uptake modeling in assessing the decarbonization potential of alternative binders, and provide a basis for justifying the capability of these binders for use as building carbon sinks.

articles.title:
Pesticides
and Tire-Derived
Chemicals in Urban Stormwater
Ponds: Spatiotemporal Dynamics, Co-Occurrence, and Implications for
Environmental Monitoring
articles.abstract: Abstract Urban stormwater contains complex mixtures of tire-derived chemicals, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and other contaminants of emerging concern, yet traditional active monitoring of urban stormwater runoff is severely constrained by precipitation events, high sampling risks, and localized spatial biases. This study evaluates whether stormwater retention ponds serve as passive, spatial–temporal integrators of urban pesticides and tire-derived chemical fingerprints. A regional survey of 13 (sub)urban stormwater retention ponds and year-long, biweekly sampling of a subset of four ponds was combined to characterize the distribution, occurrence, spatial signatures, and temporal dynamics of urban pesticides, tire-derived chemicals, and metformin. Contaminant concentrations in the ponds were similar to those previously observed in stormwater runoff. Distinct temporal dynamics were observed among contaminant classes. Tire-derived chemicals displayed concentration peaks in early spring, whereas peak concentrations of pesticides were detected in early summer. Principal component analysis and Spearman correlations revealed that tire-derived chemicals and urban pesticides co-occurred spatially and temporally. Redundancy analysis and linear mixed-effects models indicated that the spatial distributions of contaminants can be partly explained by land use types within drainage areas. These findings successfully expand the conceptual framework of stormwater retention ponds beyond structural runoff management, establishing them as effective passive spatial–temporal integrators for tracing urban contaminants.

articles.title:
Reconciliation
through Integration: A Source-Level
Bayesian Framework for Developing Measurement-Integrated Methane Inventories
articles.abstract: Abstract Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically reconcile this divergence by treating BU and TD data as independent estimates of a single true quantity to be adjusted toward agreement, rather than as evidence that each captures only part of a more complex underlying system. This complexity arises from methane emissions being strongly governed by equipment operational state and therefore instantaneous aerial “snapshots” translate poorly to annual inventories. We argue instead that BU and TD are complementary sources of evidence that should be integrated. We present a source-level Bayesian framework that constructs BU prior distributions for each emission source category and updates them with attributed aerial detections through an empirical data-augmentation procedure. The resulting posterior distributions were propagated through unit-level activity data and source-specific information via Monte Carlo simulation to produce annual estimates. Across 64 compressor stations, measurement-integrated annual estimates were 84% higher than the BU inventory, a difference driven almost entirely by compressor vents (rod packing and seal vents) and leakage through blowdown and isolation valves, which together accounted for 90% of the asset-level revision. The revision was heterogeneous across stations and source categories, emphasizing the importance of source-level, station-specific integration when developing an emissions inventory.
